description: Social Engineering Village at DEF CON 25 covers human-layer security, manipulation techniques, and defensive strategies. The 12 talks explore phishing, psychological manipulation, red team operations, and building organizational resilience.

talks.title: Nor Lose The Common Touch
talks.teaser: Master the art of building genuine rapport—a critical skill for successful social engineering attacks and red team operations.

talks.title: Beyond Phishing – Building & Sustaining a Corporate SE Program
talks.teaser: Design and sustain effective corporate social engineering programs to build organizational resilience through continuous ethical testing and training.

talks.title: Thematic Social Engineering
talks.teaser: Move beyond point-in-time social engineering tests with thematic campaigns that target specific workflows and behavioral patterns for more effective security assessment.

talks.title: Heavy Diving For Credentials
talks.teaser: Deep analysis of phishing campaign techniques, credential harvesting methods, and OSINT strategies for conducting targeted social engineering exercises.

talks.title: Social Engineering With Web Analytics
talks.teaser: Leverage web analytics platforms to identify and exploit organizational reconnaissance gaps, discovering vulnerability patterns through legitimate analytics data.

talks.title: Strategies on Securing Your Banks and Enterprises
talks.teaser: Examine your organization from an attacker's perspective—how red teamers scout websites, employees, and systems to identify and exploit security weaknesses.

talks.title: Hackers Gonna Hack , But Do They Know Why?
talks.teaser: Explore the psychological motivations driving hackers—connecting behavioral science with security research to understand why attackers target social engineering vectors.

talks.title: SE vs Predator: Using SE In Ways I Never Thought
talks.teaser: Apply social engineering skills defensively to identify predatory behavior, protect vulnerable individuals, and develop creative security applications beyond traditional penetration testing.

talks.title: Skills For A Red Teamer
talks.teaser: Master the essential skills for hybrid security assessments that combine physical, technical, and social engineering vectors into comprehensive red team operations.

talks.title: John Nye -The Human Factor  Why Are We So Bad at Security
speakers: John Nye -The Human Factor  Why Are We So Bad at Security
talks.teaser: Understand how human perception and decision-making science explains why we struggle with security—and how behavioral insights can create more effective security professionals.

talks.title: Are You Killing Your Security Program?
talks.teaser: Evaluate how organizational practices and behavioral science principles impact security program effectiveness, identifying common pitfalls in building resilient security cultures.

talks.title: Change Agents  How to Affect  Corp. Culture
talks.teaser: Transform corporate security culture through strategic change management—using principles of persuasion and organizational psychology to shift security behaviors at scale.
